title: The Making of Me - Caring for self without elevating self
speaker: Nomon Tim Burnett
summary: Nomon Tim Burnett opens with Shantideva's line that cherishing others is the source of all happiness and cherishing ourselves over others is the source of all suffering. Nomon separates self-cherishing from wise self-care, names suffering as the reliable guide, and turns to the three poisons: raga (wanting), dvesha (aversion), and moha (ignorance). Along the way come Dogen's "In aversion, weeds spread; in desire, flowers fall," the image of the self as film frames, and the claim that strong emotions fade in about forty seconds until the self regenerates them. Nomon closes with a boy in a video who asks what we practice, and proposes practicing joy.
